transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

What pushed me to come in is my eating has been really all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, eating crackers and sweets.
During those times when you're eating late at night, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you eat?
Some nights, yes. I’ll go in for a little something and then keep eating crackers and sweets for a while. Other weeks, though, I can barely bring myself to eat dinner at all.
After those times when you eat a lot at night, do you ever do anything to try to make up for the food, like making yourself throw up, taking laxatives, or exercising intensely?
No, I don’t really do anything like that afterward.
Aside from the changes in your eating, how has your mood been lately?
I’ve been kind of down in stretches. The house just feels gray and heavy, and I’ll sit at the kitchen table feeling empty, even when nothing particularly bad happened that day.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?
Yeah. Things I used to look forward to—book club, cooking, going to galleries, even tending the rose beds—just feel like chores lately. I keep putting them off.
How long have you been feeling this low and losing interest in things?
I’d say it’s been adding up to about seven months now—the gray, guilty stretches where I just don’t care about things.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this down or losing interest like this before in your life?
Yes, I’ve had stretches like this before—where everything feels gray and heavy, and I just sit there feeling empty even though nothing awful has happened.
Do these changes in your eating happen even during times when your mood is completely fine?
No, it seems tied to when I’m feeling low. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, eating crackers and sweets.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energized, wired, or on top of the world, needing very little sleep?
Yes. Sometimes I only sleep three or four hours and wake up feeling really charged, like I’m ready to write blog posts or plan projects before the sun’s even up.
When you have those periods of high energy and needing less sleep, how many days in a row do they usually last?
I’m not really sure how many days in a row. I haven’t kept track of it closely.
During those times when you felt unusually energized, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?
Yes. My thoughts can go really fast, like one idea just bumps into the next—roses, money, colors, messages, classes—and I can’t slow them down enough to explain what I mean.
During those times of high energy, did it ever cause noticeable problems with your work, relationships, or day-to-day responsibilities?

Yeah. I’ve fallen behind on my facilitator training and the work I do for my private blog, because I get too many projects going and then it’s hard to organize my thoughts or explain things clearly. It’s also caused tension at home, and that makes it harder to keep up with normal routines with my husband.
